subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Charging Standards War
description: One-minute skill: The Charging Standards War.

hook.text: For years, EV drivers faced three different charging plugs—CCS, CHAdeMO, and Tesla's proprietary NACS.

buildup.text: CCS became the standard in Europe and the US, while CHAdeMO dominated early in Japan.

discovery.text: Tesla built its own Supercharger network with a unique plug, locking out non-Tesla cars for years.

twist.text: In 2023, Ford and then nearly every automaker adopted Tesla's NACS plug as the new North American standard.

climax.text: The industry is converging on one plug—ending the confusion that slowed EV adoption for a decade.

punchline.text: It took a decade of chaos to agree on one plug shape.

quiz.question: Which charging plug did North America largely converge on in 2023?
